subject: Technical annex: evidence pack and continuity monitoring plan for high-risk deployment

Cc: Procurement <procurement@pearlview.health>

Subject: Technical annex: evidence pack and continuity monitoring plan for high-risk deployment

Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo. PearlView is preparing our internal governance package for clinical pilots and we've been asked to collect a concise technical annex that covers the following:

- Line-item mapping to NIST AI RMF (core functions + categories) and which obligations under the EU AI Act Redwood treats as platform vs. customer responsibilities (we need explicit callouts for record-keeping, human oversight, and mitigation measures).
- A deterministic description of your continuous monitoring pipeline: telemetry inputs, automated detectors, alerting thresholds, and remediation flows (including canary and fallback behavior).
- Regression testing cadence and the statistical sampling methodology you recommend for clinical prompts (power targets, sample sizes, acceptance criteria).
- A redacted example of an audit-log entry and the SOC 2 summary (we can exchange under NDA).
- Proposed SLA language for Private/VPC deployments when inference is hosted inside our VPC (latency p95/p99 targets and a documented escalation path).

Can you compile a single annex and any supporting artifacts we can attach to our RFP? Our procurement deadline is 2026-12-20. If possible please include a named technical lead who can walk our clinical risk team through the sampling methodology.

Best,
Bethany
Director, Clinical Technology
PearlView Health

Subject: Re: Technical annex: evidence pack and continuity monitoring plan for high-risk deployment

Hi Bethany  

Thanks for the clear list. I've assembled an annex and three supporting artifacts and uploaded them to the shared evidence folder. High level summary below; attachments contain the detailed mappings and test plans.

What we uploaded to Drive (links in footer):
- redwood-evidence-annex-v2.xlsx (contains row-level traceability to NIST AI RMF subcategories and EU AI Act obligations with a platform vs. customer responsibility column)
- continuity-monitoring-plan.pdf (architecture diagram, detector definitions, alert thresholds, canary/fallback behavior, and remediation SLAs)
- sla-private-deploy-addendum.pdf (templates for p95/p99 latency SLOs, maintenance windows, escalation contacts for Private/VPC)

Short answers to your bullets: 
- NIST/EU mapping: We map Redwood platform controls (inference isolation, model pinning, signed telemetry, request provenance, token-level cost accounting, and automatic fallback) to NIST core functions Govern/Map/Measure/Manage. EU AI Act obligations we consider platform-covered include technical record-keeping for model_version and inference logs, runtime mitigations (fallback and rate limiting), and basic transparency hooks. Obligations such as application-level human oversight policies, clinical label design, and training-data provenance remain customer responsibilities. The spreadsheet flags each obligation and suggests evidence artifacts.

- Continuous monitoring pipeline: We recommend a three-layer pipeline: 1) Real-time request telemetry ingestion with lightweight feature extraction; 2) Streaming anomaly detectors (population shift, latency spikes, token-distribution drift) that emit incidents when a rolling-window metric crosses a configurable threshold (default: 3 standard deviations over 24 hours); 3) An automated mitigation tier that applies canary routing to a fallback variant and notifies owners. The attached PDF includes the exact telemetry schema we expect for private deployments.

- Regression testing cadence: For high-risk clinical workloads we prescribe daily automated smoke checks, weekly stratified sampling with an A/B holdout of 5% to detect regressions with 80% power for a 5% effect size, and a monthly clinical review where clinicians review a 200-item stratified sample. Acceptance criteria and rollback gates are in the plan.

- Audit evidence & SOC 2: We can share a redacted SOC 2 Type II summary under the NDA you already have with Redwood. For RFP purposes we uploaded a redacted sample log entry demonstrating request_id, model_version, route_id, timestamp, latency_ms, and a non-reversible input_hash. Full logs are available via our compliance portal or secure transfer.

- Private/VPC SLA: The addendum contains templated p95/p99 targets and an escalation tree. For critical pilot commitments we recommend Reserved Dedicated capacity and a warm standby pool; that option is described with associated lead times and costs.

Named technical lead: Jonas Weber will run the statistical walkthrough and discuss power/sample assumptions. He's cc'd and available next week.

I'll follow up with the telemetry schema appendix and a short one-sheet describing runbook steps for remediation.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ZxY_example_RedwoodEvidencePack

Regards,
Naomi Feldman

2) How does Redwood ensure evidence integrity when we store logs on our side? Specifically, can the system sign log bundles to prove unaltered transfer?

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>

Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Technical annex: evidence pack and continuity monitoring plan for high-risk deployment

Sam 

Quick bullets to address your clinical questions: 

- Recommended alerting thresholds:
  * Population shift (KL divergence on input embeddings): alert at KL > 0.25 over a 24h rolling window; critical alarm at KL > 0.5.
  * Latency anomalies: alert at median latency > baseline + 2x IQR, critical at p99 > baseline * 1.5.
  * Output-risk heuristics (confidence heuristics / hallucination proxy): alert when top-1 confidence drops below 0.6 on a stratified sample of clinical prompts.

- Evidence integrity for on-prem logs: we support bundle signing via customer KMS/HSM. When PearlView pulls logs to S3 we provide a signed manifest (SHA-256) and optional HMAC using a shared key. We also timestamp bundles with RFC-3339 stamps and include a non-reversible input_hash to allow distributional tests without exposing raw inputs.

- User-visible impact during rollback:
  * If rollback uses an immediately available fallback variant: typical user impact is minimal; transient increase in latency (p95 delta ~20-60ms) while cache cold-starts.
  * If rollback requires re-routing to another region or capacity provisioning: degradation could be higher (p95 delta up to 200-400ms) and we surface an incident banner via the API.

Implementation note: for the highest-sensitivity triage flows we recommend Reserved Dedicated pools configured with pre-warmed KV caches to minimize rollback impact.

I'll attach a short telemetry schema appendix to the Drive folder and propose three 30-minute slots for a walkthrough with Jonas next week.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Senior Software Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference
